text:
incredible book from 2009...kept seeing this on "best autobios ever" lists, almost looked out of place, but it isnt.

much credit due to co-author J.R. Moehringer who is just a dazzingly good writer, a master hand, one of the best I can remember coming across

the two of them, plus the entire team that helped put this together, transcended the genre...really isn't a sports book or tennis book at all, it covers the following topics as well as anything I've ever read:

-self-mastery/knowledge of self...the three enemies, the game + the opponent + the self: this applies for pretty much any endeavor but you have the game (in this case, say, swinging a racket). 

then you have the opponent who you are playing, sometimes even moreso than the game -- boxing, poker come to mind. 

finally, you have you against YOURSELF. you can know the game and know your opponent ice cold...but if u aren't master of self, and if u cant execute, all that other shit doesnt matter...u are ur own worst enemy.

I think of this a lot bc people see all these book recs (whether markets or otherwise), esp if younger, and are like "what order should I tackle these"

by laying it out as 3 enemies...it makes a little more sense

-"swinging the racket," the game, has to be #1, those are the fundamentals. master those first
-"know thy opponent" is second...this is more, understanding human nature and psychological/emotional biases
-"know thyself" is third and final, the hardest and the lifelong one

u cant qualify for the US Open if u cant swing the racket

then, u have all players studying one another's weaknesses

but when it comes down to the final...like agassi/sampras, its gonna come down to who is "master of self"

amazing quote in there: "the fifth set has nothing to do with tennis."

entirely about breaking your opponent's will, conditioning...stuff u see in all sports, momentum, like where your opponent throws their absolute best stuff, and u take it and ur still standing

thats when u see the look in their face, thats when u know they are broken

and thats when u smoke their fucking boots.

-success/failure 2x...internal/external...how hollow victory is, how all pain is 2x any victory: King Solomon-esque, and a ton of credit is due to Moehringer here

these are extremely complex topics to handle well and he shapes Agassi's story into these sort of eternal frameworks

the notion that, the entire world can view you as a success, ranked #1 in the world, but you look in the mirror and all you see is failure...you feel nothing

and then at the bottom when the world sees u as a failure but u dont feel that way at all

almost 0 correlation between this 4-way "mirror" for lack of a better word (success/failure/internal/external), a theme u see over and over in amazing stories like these...the way u feel abt urself is laughably disconnected from the way the world feels about you

and then the pain of failure far exceeding the thrill of victory...something u see over and over as well

losing in the finals of a slam, hurts 2x as bad as winning a slam feels

but you see this in so many other books that its not tennis specific, thats what I mean by how the book transcends the genre...tons in here directly applicable to markets, same way if u were to ask "what was jiro dreams of sushi" about, u know sushi is the absolute last thing.

more later, I rarely take notes while reading but this one had me going...tons of screenshots of quotes/excerpts....I don't think any book is a 10/10, but for the autobio genre, this is as close to a 10/10 as u will find.
